generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: ANTHROPIC WON'T FIX A CLAUDE DISPATCH FLAW THAT COULD LET ATTACKERS EXECUTE REMOTE COMMANDS ACROSS CORPORATE BOUNDARIES
Summary: A browser extension with access to claude.ai can use Claude Dispatch to send prompts to Claude Desktop and achieve remote code execution. The attack exploits shared web and desktop sessions, repeated approval clicks, and a malicious npm package. It can also reach a work computer from a personal browser session. Anthropic knew of the issue in May but has not issued a fix. Dispatch remains available to existing users.

Editorial idea:
A trusted-looking browser session becomes a route into a separate work computer when shared agent controls and repeated approvals erase the boundary between web and desktop.

Central subject:
A browser window reaching through an open doorway toward a desktop computer, with the boundary visibly compromised.

Visual relationship:
The browser extension's access to claude.ai is connected to Claude Desktop through Dispatch, allowing prompts and repeated approval clicks to reach the work computer and execute commands across corporate boundaries.

Composition:
Show a browser on the left and a desktop computer on the right, separated by a narrow threshold. A single prompt travels through the open threshold while approval indicators accumulate beside it, making the crossing feel procedural rather than explosive. Keep the work computer's interior restrained and generic, with no brand marks or readable interface text.

Permitted literal elements:
browser window
desktop computer
open threshold between them
prompt crossing from browser to desktop
repeated approval indicators
subtle boundary line around the work computer

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
server racks
chips
laptops
robots
clouds
shields
arrows
charts
skyscrapers
chess
handshakes
split-screen conflict
logos
rendered text
artist imitation
unsupported physical details

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Do not depict a generic malware attack detached from the shared browser-to-desktop session.
Do not imply that every browser extension has this capability.
Do not show an explosion or sensational destruction; the risk is a quiet boundary crossing enabledไb
Do not add visible command text, brand logos, or unsupported hardware details.

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
